name: vis42
description: Connect Claude to your VIS42 account. Manage counterparts, products, invoices, payables, and query your business data via GraphQL.
long_description: VIS42 is an AI-first financial and revenue management platform, built on top of an agentic system; aim to automate your business administration and focus on what matters most, scale your business. VIS42 vision is to empower entrepreneurs and business owners with a reliable agentic system that will support them in their daily operations, allowing them to focus on growth and innovation. This extension connects Claude Desktop to your VIS42 account, letting you manage your business data through natural language. Create and update clients, suppliers, products, pricing, measure units, bank accounts, contacts, VAT IDs, and addresses — all without leaving Claude.

api_token.title: API Token
api_token.description: Your VIS42 API bearer token for authentication

tools.name: get-schema
tools.description:
Returns the GraphQL schema for the VIS42 app.

    By default, returns a compact type index showing all types, their fields, and relationships.
    This index is designed to be quickly scannable so you can identify what to query.

    Pass `full: true` to get the complete SDL schema with full field descriptions.

    The response includes a TERMINOLOGY GLOSSARY mapping business domain terms to GraphQL type names:
    - Invoice / Bill of sale  → Receivable (sub-type: ReceivableInvoice)
    - Quote / Estimate        → Receivable (sub-type: ReceivableQuote)
    - Credit Note             → Receivable (sub-type: ReceivableCreditNote)
    - Bill / AP Invoice       → Payable (sub-type: PayableInvoice)
    - Customer / Vendor       → Counterpart
    - Entry point             → Query { me { currentBusiness { receivables, payables, counterparts, products, expenses } } }

    Use `search-schema` to get full details for a specific type.

tools.name: search-schema
tools.description:
Search the GraphQL schema for a specific type by name or business domain alias.
    Returns the full type definition(s) with field descriptions and related sub-types.

    Accepts both GraphQL type names and plain business domain terms:
    - "Invoice" or "invoice"       → Receivable + ReceivableInvoice + ReceivableInvoiceStatus + ReceivableLineItem
    - "Quote" or "quote"           → Receivable + ReceivableQuote + ReceivableQuoteStatus + ReceivableLineItem
    - "CreditNote" or "creditnote" → Receivable + ReceivableCreditNote + ReceivableCreditNoteStatus + ReceivableLineItem
    - "Bill" or "Payable"          → Payable + PayableInvoice + PayableLineItem + related types
    - "Customer", "Vendor", "Counterpart" → Counterpart + all sub-types
    - "Product"                    → Product + ProductPrice + ProductBarcode + ProductInventory + MeasureUnit
    - "Expense"                    → Expense + ExpenseLineItem + ExpenseReceipt + CostCenter
    - "Business"                   → Business + all sub-types
    - Any GraphQL type name (e.g. "Address", "Currency", "ExchangeRate")

    Use `get-schema` to retrieve the compact type index when you need a full overview.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Executes a GraphQL query.

tools.name: action-store-business
tools.description:
Create a new business.

When a user first registers, they must create a business if me.CurrentBusiness is null.
When a user has already a business, they can create additional businesses.
A user can create multiple businesses and switch between them.
A business can represent a company or a sole proprietorship.
Depending on the business’s country, it may have both tax and VAT IDs or only one of them.
In some countries, the tax ID is the same as VAT ID.
Whether a business’s tax ID and VAT ID are required on an invoice for it to be compliant depends on several factors,
for example, the transaction type (e.g. B2B or B2C) or whether the sale is local or cross-border.
Providing both the tax ID and VAT ID for businesses helps reduce potential validation errors when issuing invoices.
## The business's incorporation number.
Also referred as Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer (UID) / Numéro d’identification des entreprises (IDE) / Numero d’identificazione delle imprese (IDI), or Repertorio Economico Amministrativo (REA).
This is a unique identifier assigned to the business upon registration/incorporation in its country. E.g., CHE-123.456.789 for Switzerland, 12345678901 for Italy
- Switzerland (CH): The UID/IDI/IDE is the incorporation number., E.g., CHE-123.456.789
- Italy (IT): The REA/CCIAA, is the incorporation number., E.g., B001234567
## The business's tax ID
- Switzerland (CH): The UID/IDI/IDE is the tax ID and also the VAT number., E.g., CHE-123.456.789 and CHE-123.456.789 IVA/TVA/MWST
- Italy (IT): The Partita IVA is the tax ID and also the VAT number., E.g., 12345678901 and IT12345678901

tools.name: action-update-business
tools.description: Update the user's current business details.

tools.name: action-store-business-bank-account
tools.description:
Create a new business bank account.
Required to complete the business onboarding.
Only one default bank account is allowed per business.
A business can have multiple bank accounts in different currencies.
Once a bank account is created in a specific currency, it CANNOT be changed to another currency.

tools.name: action-update-business-bank-account
tools.description:
Update an existing business bank account.
Only manual bank accounts can be edited. Open Banking accounts are managed automatically via TrueLayer.
Only one default bank account is allowed per business.
A business can have multiple bank accounts in different currencies.
Once a bank account is created in a specific currency, it CANNOT be changed to another currency.

tools.name: action-store-business-vat-id
tools.description:
Create a new business VAT ID. Required to complete business onboarding.
Tax ID vs VAT ID distinction:
- Tax ID (TIN): The primary tax identification number stored in the tax_id field on the business. Validated by TaxIdHelper using country-code-based regex patterns (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2). Patterns sourced from EU Commission TIN Notice (CELEX 52016XC1223(02)).
- VAT ID: A separate VAT registration number stored via this tool. Validated by VatIdHelper using VAT-type-based patterns (e.g. eu_vat, ch_vat). VAT IDs typically include a country prefix (e.g. DE123456789, CHE-123.456.789 MWST).
Depending on the country, a business may have both a tax ID and a VAT ID, or the two may overlap:
- Switzerland (CH): The UID/IDI/IDE (CHE-123.456.789) is both the tax ID and the base of the VAT number (CHE-123.456.789 MWST/TVA/IVA).
- Italy (IT): The Partita IVA (11 digits) serves as both tax ID and VAT number (prefixed IT for EU VAT).
- Germany (DE): The Steueridentifikationsnummer (11 digits, no prefix) is the tax ID; the VAT number is DE + 9 digits.
- EU countries: Most have separate national TINs and EU VAT numbers with country prefix.
Providing both tax ID and VAT ID helps reduce validation errors when issuing invoices, especially for cross-border B2B transactions.

tools.name: action-update-business-vat-id
tools.description:
Update an existing business VAT ID.

**Tax ID vs VAT ID distinction:**
- **Tax ID** (TIN): The primary tax identification number stored in the `tax_id` field on the business. Validated by `TaxIdHelper` with country-code-based patterns from the EU Commission TIN Notice.
- **VAT ID**: A separate VAT registration number managed by this tool. Validated by `VatIdHelper` with VAT-type-based patterns (e.g., `eu_vat`, `ch_vat`).

Key country examples:
- **Switzerland (CH)**: UID/IDI/IDE (CHE-123.456.789) is the tax ID; VAT number appends suffix (CHE-123.456.789 MWST/TVA/IVA).
- **Italy (IT)**: Partita IVA (11 digits) is both tax ID and VAT number (prefixed IT for EU VAT).
- **Germany (DE)**: Tax ID is 11-digit Steueridentifikationsnummer (no prefix); VAT number is DE + 9 digits.
- **EU countries**: Dual-format countries (BE, BG, EE, FI, FR, HU, IE, LT, LU, MT, NL, PL, RO, SE) may have different TIN formats for natural persons vs. companies.

tools.name: action-store-business-payment-term
tools.description:
Create a new business payment term.
Business's payment terms define the timeframe within which one has to pay a receivable invoice (for example, 30 days from the invoice issue date).
Business's payment terms structure has three tiers. The final term is required in all payment terms. This tier defines the receivable invoice's due date and does not support discounts.

tools.name: store-product
tools.description:
Create a new product or service.
The Product object represents the specific services, materials, or physical or digital goods sold.
A business must have at least one product configured in order to create any receivables.
Products can be of type "product" or "service", a product must have at least one default price.
When creating a new product or service, the price defined during creation is automatically set as the default price.
In the context of receivables, products are used to define line items, a measure unit is the standard unit used to
measure the quantity of a product or service.

tools.name: update-product
tools.description: Update an existing product or service.

tools.name: destroy-product
tools.description:
Delete an existing product or service.
A product can only be deleted if it is not associated with any receivables.

tools.name: store-product-price
tools.description:
Create a new price for a product or service.
A product can have only one price per currency.
A product must have at least one price, which is set as the default price.
Only one default price is allowed per product.

tools.name: update-product-price
tools.description: Update an existing price for a product or service.

tools.name: destroy-product-price
tools.description:
Delete an existing price for a product or service.
A price can only be deleted if it is not set as the default price for the product.
If the price to be deleted is the default price, another price must first be set as the default price.

tools.name: store-product-barcode
tools.description:
Create a new barcode for a product.
A product can have multiple barcodes, but each barcode must be unique within the business.
Supported barcode types are EAN-13, UPC-A, UPC-E, and QR Code.

tools.name: update-product-barcode
tools.description:
Update an existing barcode for a product.
The barcode value and type can be changed. The new barcode must be unique within the business.

tools.name: destroy-product-barcode
tools.description: Delete an existing barcode from a product.

tools.name: store-product-inventory
tools.description:
Create inventory tracking for a product.
A product can only have one inventory record. Only products of type "product" support inventory (not services).
Inventory tracks quantity on hand, reserved quantity, and optional reorder thresholds.

tools.name: update-product-inventory
tools.description:
Update the inventory record for a product.
Adjusts quantity on hand, reserved quantity, and reorder thresholds.

tools.name: destroy-product-inventory
tools.description: Delete the inventory record for a product.

tools.name: store-measure-unit
tools.description:
Create a new measure unit.
A measure unit can be associated with multiple products.
Examples of measure units: meters, kilograms, pieces, hours.

tools.name: update-measure-unit
tools.description: Update an existing measure unit.

tools.name: destroy-measure-unit
tools.description:
Delete an existing measure unit.
A measure unit can only be deleted if it is not associated with any products.

tools.name: store-counterpart-organization
tools.description:
Create a new counterpart (supplier or client).
Counterparts represent the suppliers and clients of a business.
A counterpart must be created before a business can create receivables and payables.
The counterpart's default address is normally used for invoicing and tax purposes, and referenced as billing address in invoices.
Depending on the counterpart’s country, it may have both tax and VAT IDs or only one of them. In some countries, the tax ID is the same as VAT ID.
A common compliance requirement for certain transaction types is to include the customer’s tax ID or VAT ID in invoices, if available. For example, intra-EU B2B sales require the customer’s VAT ID in invoices.
How to check if tax ID or VAT ID is required: require at least one of tax ID or VAT ID specified. If the counterpart is registered for VAT, we expect that the VAT ID is specified. If the counterpart is not VAT-registered, then tax ID is required.
What is a tax ID:
Also referred as Tax Identification Number (TIN), or Fiscal Code.
- Switzerland (CH):
    - The UID/IDI/IDE is the tax ID and also the VAT number., E.g., CHE-123.456.789 and CHE-123.456.789 IVA/TVA/MWST
- Italy (IT):
    - The Partita IVA is the tax ID and also the VAT number., E.g., 12345678901 and IT12345678901

tools.name: store-counterpart-individual
tools.description:
Create a new counterpart (supplier or client).
Counterparts represent the suppliers and clients of a business.
A counterpart must be created before a business can create receivables and payables.
The counterpart's default address is normally used for invoicing and tax purposes, and referenced as billing address in invoices.
Depending on the counterpart’s country, it may have both tax and VAT IDs or only one of them. In some countries, the tax ID is the same as VAT ID.
A common compliance requirement for certain transaction types is to include the customer’s tax ID or VAT ID in invoices, if available. For example, intra-EU B2B sales require the customer’s VAT ID in invoices.
How to check if tax ID or VAT ID is required: generally do not require a tax ID but may require a VAT ID.
What is a tax ID:
Also referred as Tax Identification Number (TIN), or Fiscal Code.
- Switzerland (CH):
    - The AVS/OASI number is the tax ID and VAT number defined as 756.XXXX.YYYY.ZZ = 10 numerals., E.g., 756.1234.5678.97
- Italy (IT):
    - The Codice Fiscale is the tax ID and VAT number defined as LLLLLL99L99L999L = 6 letters + 2 numerals + 1 letter + 2 numerals + 1 letter + 3 numerals + 1 letter., E.g., RSSMRA85M01H501U

tools.name: update-counterpart-organization
tools.description: Update an existing organization counterpart (business).

tools.name: destroy-counterpart
tools.description:
Delete an existing counterpart (supplier or client).
A counterpart can only be deleted if it is not associated with any receivables or payables.

tools.name: store-counterpart-bank-account
tools.description:
Create a new bank account for a counterpart.
Only one default bank account is allowed per counterpart.
A counterpart can have multiple bank accounts in different currencies.
Once a bank account is created in a specific currency, it CANNOT be changed to another currency.

tools.name: update-counterpart-bank-account
tools.description: Update an existing bank account for a counterpart.

tools.name: update-counterpart-individual
tools.description: Update an existing individual counterpart (person).

tools.name: destroy-counterpart-bank-account
tools.description: Delete an existing bank account for a counterpart.

tools.name: store-counterpart-contact
tools.description:
Create a new contact for a counterpart.
A counterpart can have multiple contacts.
Contacts are normally used when a counterpart is an organization, and the contacts are the individuals
working at that organization.

tools.name: update-counterpart-contact
tools.description: Update an existing contact for a counterpart.

tools.name: destroy-counterpart-contact
tools.description: Delete an existing contact for a counterpart.

tools.name: destroy-counterpart-vat-id
tools.description: Delete an existing VAT ID for a counterpart. This removes only the VAT ID record; the counterpart's primary tax_id field is not affected.

tools.name: store-counterpart-address
tools.description:
Create a new address for a counterpart.
Only one default address is allowed per counterpart.
A counterpart can have multiple addresses.

tools.name: update-counterpart-address
tools.description: Update an existing address for a counterpart.

tools.name: destroy-counterpart-address
tools.description: Delete an existing address for a counterpart.

tools.name: store-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Create a new payable invoice. Payable invoices are created with the status DRAFT.
Accounts payable refers to the money a business owes to its suppliers or vendors for products or
services that have been received but have yet to be paid for by the company.
A payable invoice is a document received from a supplier or vendor that lists the products or services
the company received and the amount due to the supplier or vendor.
Each payable invoice is allocated with a status that indicates its progress throughout the payable lifecycle,
from its creation until its payment.

tools.name: update-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Update an existing payable invoice. Only DRAFT payable invoices can be updated.
Accounts payable refers to the money a business owes to its suppliers or vendors for products or
services that have been received but have yet to be paid for by the company.

tools.name: mark-as-new-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable invoice to **New**.
    A payable invoice can only be set to **NEW** when it is in a DRAFT or REFUSED state.

tools.name: approval-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable invoice to **Approval Pending**.
    A payable invoice can only be set to **APPROVAL PENDING** when it is in a NEW state.
    When a payable invoice is being set to **APPROVAL PENDING**, an approval request is sent to the approver.

tools.name: approve-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable invoice to **Approved**.
A payable invoice can only be set to **APPROVED** when it is in an APPROVAL PENDING state.
When a payable invoice is being set to **APPROVED**, it means that the approver has reviewed and approved the invoice for payment.

tools.name: refuse-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable invoice to **Refused**.
A payable invoice can only be set to **REFUSED** when it is in an APPROVAL PENDING state.
When a payable invoice is being set to **REFUSED**, it means that the approver has reviewed and rejected the invoice.

tools.name: cancel-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable invoice to **Cancelled**.
A payable invoice can only be set to **CANCELLED** when it is in a NEW state.

tools.name: mark-as-paid-payable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable invoice to **Paid**.
    A payable invoice can only be set to **PAID** when it is in an APPROVED state.

tools.name: store-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Create a new payable credit note. Payable credit notes are created with the status DRAFT.
A payable credit note is a document received from a supplier or vendor that reduces the amount owed
on a previously issued payable invoice. Credit notes are used to correct billing errors, account for
returned goods, or adjust the amount due for services not fully delivered.
Each credit note must reference a payable invoice via the `based_on` field, which is the UUID of the
referenced invoice payable.

tools.name: update-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Update an existing payable credit note. Only DRAFT payable credit notes can be updated.
A payable credit note is a document received from a supplier or vendor that reduces the amount owed
on a previously issued payable invoice.

tools.name: mark-as-new-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable credit note to **New**.
    A payable credit note can only be set to **NEW** when it is in a DRAFT or REFUSED state.

tools.name: approval-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable credit note to **Approval Pending**.
    A payable credit note can only be set to **APPROVAL PENDING** when it is in a NEW state.
    When a payable credit note is being set to **APPROVAL PENDING**, an approval request is sent to the approver.

tools.name: approve-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable credit note to **Approved**.
A payable credit note can only be set to **APPROVED** when it is in an APPROVAL PENDING state.
When a payable credit note is being set to **APPROVED**, it means that the approver has reviewed and approved the credit note for application.

tools.name: reject-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable credit note to **Refused**.
A payable credit note can only be set to **REFUSED** when it is in an APPROVAL PENDING state.
When a payable credit note is being set to **REFUSED**, it means that the approver has reviewed and rejected the credit note.

tools.name: cancel-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable credit note to **Cancelled**.
A payable credit note can only be set to **CANCELLED** when it is in a NEW state.

tools.name: apply-payable-credit-note
tools.description:
Apply an existing payable credit note. Applying a credit note transitions it to the **Applied** status.
A payable credit note can only be applied when it is in an APPROVED state.
When a credit note is applied, it reduces the outstanding amount on the referenced payable invoice.
If the credit note fully covers the remaining balance of the referenced invoice, the invoice may be
automatically transitioned to the **Paid** status.

tools.name: destroy-payable
tools.description:
Delete an existing payable.
A payable can ONLY be deleted when it is in a DRAFT state.

tools.name: store-payable-purchase-order
tools.description:
Create a new payable purchase order (PO). Purchase orders are created with the status DRAFT.
A purchase order is a document the business sends to a supplier or vendor detailing the products or services
the company wishes to purchase, including quantities and agreed-upon prices.
Once a purchase order is issued, it cannot be modified. Use the issue-payable-purchase-order tool to
change the status from DRAFT to ISSUED and optionally send the PO to the supplier by email.
Prerequisites:
- A counterpart: a purchase order must specify a supplier, which can be an individual or an organization.
- At least one line item specifying the products or services to be purchased.

tools.name: update-payable-purchase-order
tools.description:
Update an existing payable purchase order. Only DRAFT purchase orders can be updated.
Once issued, a purchase order cannot be modified.

tools.name: issue-payable-purchase-order
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing payable purchase order to **Issued**.
A purchase order can only be set to **ISSUED** when it is in a DRAFT state.
When a purchase order is issued, it means it has been sent to the supplier for fulfillment.
Use `transfer_method = manual` to mark the PO as issued without sending an email.
Use `transfer_method = email` to issue the PO and send it to the supplier by email (requires the `email` object with at least `to` and `subject`).
Once issued, a purchase order cannot be modified.

tools.name: store-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Create a new receivable invoice. Receivables are created with the status DRAFT.
Accounts receivable refers to the money owed to a business by its clients for products or
services that have been delivered but have yet to be paid for by the clients.
An invoice is a request for payment that lists the products or services the business delivered and the amount due.
Each receivable is allocated with a status that indicates its progress throughout the receivable lifecycle,
from its creation until its payment.
Once the receivable invoice is finalized and ISSUED to the counterpart, it cannot be modified. In case changes
are needed, a credit note must be ISSUED to correct the original receivable invoice, and if necessary, a new receivable invoice can be created.
A credit note reduces the amount due on an issued receivable invoice.
Prerequisites
To be able to create and issue receivables invoice, a business must have at least:
- A counterpart: a receivable needs to specify counterpart, which can be an individual or a organization. The counterpart must have at least one billing address.
- A product or service: a receivable needs to specify at least one line item that specifies the products or services provided to the counterpart.
- A VAT ID: a receivable needs to specify the VAT ID of the business.
- A bank account: a receivable also needs to specify the business bank account to which the payment should be made. This bank account must be able to accept the currency reflected on the receivable.
- A payment term: a receivable also needs to specify the business payment terms, that define the period within which the payment for the receivable must be made.

tools.name: store-receivable-quote
tools.description:
Create a new receivable quote. Receivables are created with the status DRAFT.
Accounts receivable refers to the money owed to a business by its clients for products or
services that have been delivered but have yet to be paid for by the clients.
Some of the document types used in accounts receivable are:
Each receivable is allocated with a status that indicates its progress throughout the receivable lifecycle,
from its creation until its payment.
Prerequisites
To be able to create and issue receivables quote and invoice, a business must have at least:
- A counterpart: a receivable needs to specify counterpart, which can be an individual or a organization. The counterpart must have at least one billing address.
- A product or service: a receivable needs to specify at least one line item that specifies the products or services provided to the counterpart.
- A VAT ID: a receivable needs to specify the VAT ID of the business.

tools.name: update-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Update an existing receivable invoice. Invoices can only be updated when they are in DRAFT status.
Accounts receivable refers to the money owed to a business by its clients for products or
services that have been delivered but have yet to be paid for by the clients.
An invoice is a request for payment that lists the products or services the business delivered and the amount due.
Each receivable is allocated with a status that indicates its progress throughout the receivable lifecycle,
from its creation until its payment.
Once the receivable invoice is finalized and ISSUED to the counterpart, it cannot be modified. In case changes
are needed, a credit note must be ISSUED to correct the original receivable invoice, and if necessary, a new receivable invoice can be created.
A credit note reduces the amount due on an issued receivable invoice.

tools.name: update-receivable-quote
tools.description:
Update an existing receivable quote. Quotes can only be updated when they are in DRAFT status.
Accounts receivable refers to the money owed to a business by its clients for products or
services that have been delivered but have yet to be paid for by the clients.
A quote is a formal offer that details how much the products or services will cost before the client commits to a purchase.
Each receivable is allocated with a status that indicates its progress throughout the receivable lifecycle,
from its creation until its payment.
Prerequisites
To be able to create and issue receivables quote and invoice, a business must have at least:
- A counterpart: a receivable needs to specify counterpart, which can be an individual or a organization. The counterpart must have at least one billing address.
- A product or service: a receivable needs to specify at least one line item that specifies the products or services provided to the counterpart.
- A VAT ID: a receivable needs to specify the VAT ID of the business.

tools.name: destroy-receivable
tools.description:
Delete an existing receivable.
A receivable can only be deleted if it is in a DRAFT state.

tools.name: issue-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing receivable invoice to **Issued**.
A receivable can only be set to **ISSUED** when it is in an DRAFT state.
When a receivable is being set to **ISSUED**, it means that the receivable has been issued to the customer.

tools.name: issue-receivable-quote
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing receivable quote to **Issued**.
A receivable can only be set to **ISSUED** when it is in an DRAFT state.
When a receivable is being set to **ISSUED**, it means that the receivable has been issued to the customer.

tools.name: cancel-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing receivable to **Cancelled**.
A receivable can only be set to **CANCELLED** when it is in an **ISSUED** or **OVERDUE** state.
When a receivable is being set to **CANCELLED**, it means that the receivable is no longer valid and will not be collected.

tools.name: mark-as-paid-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing receivable invoice to **Paid**.
A receivable can only be set to **PAID** when it is in an ISSUED, OVERDUE, or PARTIALLY_PAID state.
When a receivable is being set to **PAID**, it means that the receivable has been fully paid by the counterparty.

tools.name: mark-as-partially-paid-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing receivable invoice to **Partially Paid**.
A receivable can only be set to **PARTIALLY PAID** when it is in an ISSUED, OVERDUE, or PARTIALLY_PAID state.
When a receivable is being set to **PARTIALLY PAID**, it means that the receivable has been partially paid by the counterparty.

tools.name: mark-as-uncollectible-receivable-invoice
tools.description:
Set the status of an existing receivable invoice to **Uncollectible**.
A receivable can only be set to **UNCOLLECTIBLE** when it is in an ISSUED or OVERDUE state.
When a receivable is being set to **UNCOLLECTIBLE**, it means that the receivable has been partially paid by the counterparty.

tools.name: store-expense-receipt
tools.description:
Create a new expense receipt. Expense receipts are created with the status DRAFT.
An expense receipt represents a proof of purchase or payment received from a supplier,
typically for smaller or ad-hoc purchases. Receipts can be uploaded, parsed via Document AI,
and matched to ledger transactions.
Each expense is allocated with a status that indicates its progress throughout the expense lifecycle.

tools.name: update-expense-receipt
tools.description:
Update an existing expense receipt. Only DRAFT expense receipts can be updated.
An expense receipt represents a proof of purchase or payment received from a supplier.

tools.name: destroy-expense
tools.description:
Delete an existing expense. An expense can only be deleted when it is in a DRAFT state.
This performs a soft delete — the expense can be restored later if needed.

tools.name: add-expense-line-item
tools.description:
Add a single line item to an existing expense.

Each line item represents a product or service purchased. Line items can optionally be
assigned to a cost center and a ledger account for accounting categorization.

tools.name: store-cost-center
tools.description:
Create a new cost center for the current business.

Cost centers are used to categorize and track expenses by department, project, or activity.
Each expense line item can be assigned to a cost center for reporting and budgeting purposes.
A cost center can be marked as external if it represents an outside entity or project.

tools.name: list-cost-centers
tools.description:
List all cost centers for the current business, paginated.
Cost centers are used to categorize and track expenses by department, project, or activity.
Use this tool to discover existing cost centers before assigning one to an expense line item.

tools.name: update-cost-center
tools.description:
Update an existing cost center.

Cost centers are used to categorize and track expenses by department, project, or activity.

tools.name: list-ledger-accounts
tools.description:
List all business bank accounts that are connected to the Formance Ledger.
Returns each account with its current balances (volumes by currency).
Optionally filter by currency code (e.g. CHF, EUR, USD).
Only accounts with an active ledger connection (ledger_id is set) are returned.

tools.name: get-ledger-account-balance
tools.description:
Get the current balance for a specific business bank account from the Formance Ledger.
The account must be connected to the ledger (has a ledger_id).
Returns volumes by currency showing input, output, and balance for the account.
Use `list-ledger-accounts` first to find valid account IDs.

tools.name: get-ledger-account-volumes
tools.description:
Get the detailed volume breakdown (input, output, balance) per asset for a specific business bank account.
Optionally filter by currency (ISO 4217 code, e.g. CHF, EUR, USD).
More granular than `get-ledger-account-balance` — shows total amounts that have flowed in and out, not just the current balance.
The account must be connected to the ledger.

tools.name: list-ledger-transactions
tools.description:
List transactions for a specific business bank account from the Formance Ledger.
The account must be connected to the ledger.
Transactions are enriched with counterpart information when available.
Results are paginated — use `page_size` to control the number of transactions returned (default: 20, max: 100).

tools.name: get-ledger-aggregated-balances
tools.description:
Get aggregated balances across all accounts in the business ledger.
Returns a summary of all balances grouped by currency across every connected bank account.
The business must have an active ledger (ledger_name is set).
Useful for getting a high-level financial overview of the business.

tools.name: get-ledger-stats
tools.description:
Get aggregate statistics for the business ledger.
Returns total account count and transaction count.
Useful for a quick dashboard summary of ledger activity.
The business must have an active ledger (ledger_name is set).

tools.name: record-ledger-transaction
tools.description:
Record a financial transaction in the Formance Ledger for a business bank account.
Transactions are between a business bank account and a counterpart bank account.
Direction determines the money flow:
- `false` (incoming): money flows from the counterpart account into the business bank account (e.g. payment received).
- `true` (outgoing): money flows from the business bank account to the counterpart account (e.g. payment sent).
The business bank account must be connected to the ledger.
Amount is a decimal value (e.g. 1500.50) that will be converted to minor units internally.
A unique reference is auto-generated if not provided.

tools.name: revert-ledger-transaction
tools.description:
Revert a previously recorded ledger transaction by its numeric ID.
Creates a compensating transaction that reverses the original postings — the original transaction is NOT deleted.
The account must be connected to the ledger.
Use `list-ledger-transactions` to find the transaction ID to revert.

tools.name: create-business-ledger
tools.description:
Create a Formance Ledger for the current business.
A business must have a ledger before bank accounts can be connected to it.
This is a one-time setup operation — if the business already has a ledger, the operation succeeds silently.
The ledger name is generated from the business ID (format: `business_{uuid}`).
After creation, use `connect-account-to-ledger` to connect individual bank accounts.

tools.name: connect-account-to-ledger
tools.description:
Connect a business bank account to the Formance Ledger for double-entry bookkeeping.
The business must already have a ledger created (use `create-business-ledger` first).
If the account is already connected, the operation succeeds silently.
Once connected, the account can receive transactions via `record-ledger-transaction`
and its balances can be queried via `get-ledger-account-balance`.

tools.name: link-payment
tools.description:
Link a ledger transaction to a document (expense, payable, or receivable) as a payment.
Creates a payment link record. Does NOT change the document's status — use the
appropriate status transition tools after linking (e.g., mark-as-paid-receivable-invoice).

tools.name: unlink-payment
tools.description:
Remove a payment link from a document. This hard-deletes the payment link record.
Does NOT change the document's status — update it separately if needed.

tools.name: list-unreconciled
tools.description:
List documents that are not fully reconciled against ledger transactions.

Covers expenses, payable invoices/credit notes, and receivable invoices/credit notes.
Supports filtering by type, currency, counterpart, and date range.

tools.name: suggest-matches
tools.description:
Suggest ledger transactions that may match a given document.

Candidates are ranked by amount, counterpart, and date proximity, and returned with
confidence scores. Exact matches (score 1.0) can be auto-linked; ambiguous matches
should be presented to the user for confirmation.

tools.name: get-payment-status
tools.description:
Get the payment reconciliation status for a document.

Returns the payment status (unpaid, partial, paid, overpaid), paid amount,
outstanding amount, and all linked payments.

tools.name: auto-reconcile-batch
tools.description:
Auto-reconcile all unmatched documents against ledger transactions.
Runs synchronously and returns per-document results with match details.
Only exact matches (confidence >= threshold) are auto-linked.
Returns each document with its match result, counterpart, amount, and status.

tools.name: upload-document-file
tools.description:
Uploads a document file to storage, and associates it with a document.
    A document can be either a receivable or a payable, depending on the `type` parameter.
    How to use:
    - Files are uploaded by the user during a conversation.
    - The file's external ID is passed as the `file_id` parameter.
    - The `type` parameter specifies whether the document is a receivable or a payable.
    - The `id` parameter is the ID (UUID) of the document to associate the file with.
    - The tool retrieves the file from storage and associates it with the specified document.

tools.name: get-document-url
tools.description:
Allow to retrieves documents URL from storage. Documents can be either receivables or payables.
How to use:
- The tool accepts an array of documents, each with an `id` and `type
- IDs can be found using the GraphQL tools if not provided directly.
- ALWAYS search for the receivables/payables IDs (UUID) when you are not provided with them, using the GraphQL
  tools. Normally receivables/payables are referenced via the `document_id` field; when you are provided with a list
  of document IDs, you can assume they are `document_id`s. ALWAYS search for the IDs (UUID) using the GraphQL tools
  when you are not provided with them.
- If multiple documents are needed, retrieve all URLs in a single call.

tools.name: document-to-json
tools.description:
Converts a PDF document to JSON using Google Document AI.
    How to use:
    - Provide the `file_id` (external ID of the uploaded PDF file).
    - Provide the `type` to select the appropriate processor:
      - `invoice`: uses the invoice-parser processor to extract payable invoice entities.
      - `bank_statement`: uses the bank-statement processor to extract transactions, balances, IBAN, and currency.
      - `receipt`: uses the expense-receipt processor to extract receipt entities (supplier, amounts, line items, dates).
    - After parsing an invoice, use the returned entities to create or pre-fill a payable.
    - After parsing a bank statement, use `record-ledger-transaction` to record each extracted transaction.
    - After parsing a receipt, use the returned entities to create or update an expense.

tools.name: notification-email
tools.description: Sends a notification email to one or more recipients.

tools.name: notification-in-app
tools.description: Sends an in-app notification to one or more users.

tools.name: notification-push
tools.description: Sends a push notification to one or more users.

tools.name: notification-slack
tools.description:
Sends a notification message to a Slack channel via an incoming webhook.
The business must have Slack activated in their notification channel settings
(Business > Notifications) before this tool can be used.
If the channel is not activated or no webhook URL is configured, the tool
returns an error instructing the user to configure it.

tools.name: notification-teams
tools.description:
Sends a notification message to a Microsoft Teams channel via an incoming webhook.
The business must have Teams activated in their notification channel settings
(Business > Notifications) before this tool can be used.
If the channel is not activated or no webhook URL is configured, the tool
returns an error instructing the user to configure it.

tools.name: get-headers
tools.description:
Returns the column headers and all sheet names from an uploaded spreadsheet file.
    Use this tool first to understand the structure of a file before calling `read-sheet`.
    How to use:
    - Provide the `file_id` (the external ID of the uploaded file).
    - Optionally specify `sheet` (name or 0-based index) to target a specific sheet; defaults to the first sheet.
    - Returns the list of column headers, the active sheet name, and all sheet names in the workbook.

tools.name: read-sheet
tools.description:
Reads cell data from an uploaded spreadsheet file (XLSX, XLS, CSV, ODS).
    Returns rows keyed by column header.
    How to use:
    - Provide the `file_id` (the external ID of the uploaded file).
    - Optionally specify `sheet` (name or 0-based index) to target a specific sheet; defaults to the first sheet.
    - Optionally specify `limit` to cap the number of rows returned (default 200).
    - If the result is truncated, `truncated` will be true and you can call again with `offset` to page through.
    - Date values are automatically converted to ISO datetime strings.
    - Merged cells have their value replicated across all covered cells.

tools.name: map-columns
tools.description:
Maps raw column headers from an uploaded spreadsheet to a set of semantic target field names.
    Uses multilingual heuristics (EN/FR/DE/IT/NL/ES) with confidence scores.
    Any field with confidence below 0.70 is left in `unmapped` and returned with `raw_headers`
    so you can interpret ambiguous columns yourself before calling `read-sheet`.
    How to use:
    - Provide the `file_id` and the list of `target_fields` you want to locate.
    - Check `mapping` for high-confidence matches and `unmapped` for fields that need your judgment.

tools.name: write-sheet
tools.description:
Generate a spreadsheet file from structured data and return a pre-signed download URL.

    Produces either XLSX (default) or CSV, uploads it to storage, and returns the URL.
    How to use:
    - Provide a `title` for the spreadsheet and one or more `sheets`, each with `name`, `headers`, and `rows`.
    - Optionally set `format` to `csv` for a flat CSV output (only the first sheet is used).

tools.name: write-pdf
tools.description:
Generate a PDF from a pdfmake docDefinition and return a pre-signed download URL.

    Takes a pdfmake docDefinition object, renders it to PDF, uploads it to storage.

    How to use:
    - Provide a `title` for the PDF filename.
    - Provide a `definition` object following the pdfmake docDefinition format.
      At minimum it must contain a `content` array.
